list.title: Lower Vaccination Rates:
list.snippet: Flu shot uptake has declined since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, leaving more people vulnerable to infection.

list.title: Dominant Strains:
list.snippet: This year's flu season is characterized by the simultaneous circulation of both H1N1 and H3N2 influenza A strains, which are known to cause more severe illness in some individuals.

list.title: Waning Immunity:
list.snippet: With reduced social interaction and increased mask-wearing during the pandemic, some experts suggest that immunity to the flu may have decreased in the general population, making more people susceptible.

list.title: Increased Social Activity:
list.snippet: As pandemic restrictions have eased, people are spending more time in public spaces like schools and workplaces, increasing opportunities for the virus to spread.

list.title: Co-infections:
list.snippet: The concurrent circulation of other respiratory viruses like RSV and Rhinovirus alongside the flu can lead to more severe illness and prolonged recovery.
